summary.note: No REJECT found. The slice is dominated by ONE mechanically diagnosable defect class (the script's default +ar fired on final-stressed loanwords that take -er), plus the brief's own documented classes (vowel-final neuter -> -n; consonant-final neuter -> zero; umlaut; -el/-er syncope; double plurals). Every 'to' value in the slice is a real Swedish form -- I scanned all 84 for the 'Lagerar' failure and found none. Crucially, the first round did NOT blanket-apply -er: it correctly kept -ar (with syncope) for the -el/-er stems (aster->astrar, ceder->cedrar, iller->illrar, mixer->mixrar, hummer->humrar, bagel->baglar, bulldozer->bulldozrar) and -or for ros/mossa, reserving -er for the final-stressed loans. That is the discrimination the brief demands, and it holds throughout.

systematicFindings.detail: The brief asks me to check systematically whether the first round fixed one field but not its coupled partner. All five keys in this slice whose plural becomes a neuter zero plural (beach-umbrella/Parasoll, cast/Gips, fig/Fikon, bowling-ball/Bowlingklot, camp/Lager) carry a matching gender correction n->t. No coupling oversight found in this slice.

systematicFindings.finding: A SUPPORTING ARGUMENT USED IN THREE 'why' TEXTS IS FALSE (does not change the verdicts)
systematicFindings.detail: cabbage, cauliflower and chameleon each argue that 'zero plural is a NEUTER property' / 'an utrum noun cannot have a zero plural'. That is false in Swedish: -are and -er agent nouns are utrum with a zero plural (en larare -> flera larare; en musiker -> flera musiker). The data proves it against itself -- sister key 'mechanic' is stored as Mekaniker/Mekaniker (utrum, zero plural) and is CORRECT. The conclusions still stand (kal, blomkal and kameleont are in none of those classes), so I confirm all three, but the reasoning should not be reused as a rule elsewhere in the audit.

systematicFindings.finding: DIACRITIC LOSS IN SISTER KEYS -- OUTSIDE MY SLICE, BUT REAL
systematicFindings.detail: My 84 'to' values are all diacritically intact (checked programmatically). But four proposed plural values later in the alphabet strip a diacritic and produce non-words: scrubs -> 'Sjukhusklader' (should be Sjukhuskläder), push-pin -> 'Haftstift' (should be Häftstift), purse -> 'Portmonnaer' (should be Portmonnäer), sauce -> 'Saser' (should be Såser -- 'Saser' is not a Swedish word at all). These are exactly the 'beanie/Mossa' corruption class the first round itself identified, reappearing inside its own corrections. Flagged here for the reviewer of that slice / the operator; I have not judged them, they are not mine. It bears directly on my hospital-gown ESCALATE (its sister key is scrubs).

systematicFindings.finding: PRE-EXISTING DUPLICATE PAIRS ARE NOT CREATED BY THESE FIXES
systematicFindings.detail: beach-umbrella/parasol, bow/rosette and bathing-suit/swimsuit are each already byte-identical rows in the current data (all N6-flagged). The corrections treat each pair consistently (parasol->Parasoll, rosette->Rosetter, swimsuit->Baddräkter all exist), so the fixes neither create nor worsen the duplication. Per brief rule 7 I checked whether 'to' would MAKE a row identical to a sister key: it would not -- the identity predates the correction. Confirmed rather than escalated.

rows.note: SAOL: ambulans ~en ~er. En ambulans -> flera ambulanser; final-stressed -ans loans take -er. 'Ambulansar' is the script's +ar default and is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: antilop ~en ~er. Final-stressed loan -> -er. 'Antilopar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: paj ~en ~er, hence äppelpaj -> äppelpajer. Consistent with the sibling key 'pie' in the same correction set. 'Appelpajar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: fåtölj ~en ~er. The 'to' value carries the diacritics correctly (Fåtöljer) even though the 'why' prose writes the stem unaccented -- the value, not the prose, is what ships. Confirmed.

SAOL: aster ~n, pl. astrar. Unstressed -er stem syncopates and takes -ar (syster->systrar, åker->åkrar). Note the first round correctly did NOT apply -er here -- it discriminated. 'Asterar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: asteroid ~en ~er. 'Asteroidar' is the script's default and is not a Swedish word.

SAOL: avokado ~n ~r -> avokador. NOTE this is one of two keys in the slice whose current value ('Avokados') was NOT script-generated -- the script's default would have been *Avokadoar -- so a human or a source wrote the English -s plural deliberately. I tested this as a possible 'lego' case (a correction deleting an attested form) and reject that reading: 'avokados' circulates colloquially but avokador is the Swedish declension form, and the first round says so honestly.
SAOL: overall ~en ~er, hence babyoverall -> babyoveraller. 'Babyoverallar' is not a Swedish word.

The slice's closest call, tested hard as a possible 'lego' REJECT. Like avocado, the current 'Bagels' was NOT script-generated (the default would be *Bagelar/Baglar), so someone wrote the English plural deliberately -- that is the lego signal and it deserved the test. It survives the test: unlike keps/kex/muffins (borrowed INTO Swedish as singulars from English plurals), 'bagel' was borrowed as a singular (en bagel), so its plural must be formed by Swedish rules, and the -el syncope is fully productive (cykel->cyklar, nyckel->nycklar, pixel->pixlar) -> baglar. CAVEAT, stated honestly: I am not quoting a SAOL entry verbatim and cannot exclude that ~s is listed as a variant. It does not change the verdict, because 'Baglar' is unambiguously a correct Swedish form -- so applying the fix cannot corrupt the data, which is the test the lego case actually failed. The first round's claim that 'Bagels' is 'not a Swedish plural form at all' is the overstated part, not the fix.
SAOL: baguette ~n ~r -> baguetter. 'Baguettar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: ballong ~en ~er. Final-stressed -ong loan -> -er. 'Ballongar' is not a Swedish word.

SAOL: dräkt ~en ~er, hence baddräkt -> baddräkter. N6 checked: sister key 'swimsuit' is an identical row already and is corrected identically (-> Baddräkter), so the fix keeps the pair consistent and creates no new duplicate.

ett parasoll, parasollet -> flera parasoll. Consonant-final neuter = zero plural (cf. ett hotell/kapell -> hotell/kapell). This is a true camp/Lagerar coupled defect and the matching gender fix n->t is present -- I verified it. N6 checked: sister key 'parasol' is already a byte-identical row and is corrected identically, so the duplication predates the fix rather than being created by it (brief rule 7 does not bite).

en mössa -> flera mössor (1st declension). The plural inherited the singular's diacritic corruption (Mossa = moss), so the declension was right but applied to the wrong lemma. Coupled with the singular fix Mossa->Mössa, which must land with it.
SAOL: mixer ~n, pl. mixrar. Unstressed -er stem syncopates, takes -ar -- correctly NOT given -er by the first round. 'Mixerar' is not a Swedish word.

SAOL: rosett ~en ~er. themes=[christmas], cur.s=Rosett -> the ribbon bow reading is right (not båge/stråke). N6 checked: sister key 'rosette' is already an identical row and is corrected identically -> Rosetter; duplication is pre-existing, not created.
SAOL: klot ~et, zero plural. Ett bowlingklot -> flera bowlingklot. Coupled defect; the matching gender fix n->t is present -- verified. 'Bowlingkloter' is an invented word.
SAOL: portfölj ~en ~er. 'Portföljar' is not a Swedish word.

The -er syncope + -ar is fully productive for machine loans (container->containrar, revolver->revolvrar, trailer->trailrar) -> bulldozrar. CAVEAT: the first round honestly flags this as pattern-based rather than a quoted entry, and I make the same reservation -- I am not citing a SAOL entry for bulldozer. The verdict holds because 'Bulldozerar' is wrong under every reading (it has neither the syncope nor a valid ending), so the fix cannot make the data worse even if ~s is a listed variant.
SAOL: hytt ~en ~er, hence strandhytt -> strandhytter. 'Strandhyttar' is not a Swedish word. (The lemma 'strandhytt' for a cabana is a separate question the fix does not touch.)

NO_PLURAL accepted for the depicted sense: themes=[vegetables] shows a cabbage head, and a Swedish child counts 'två kålhuvuden', not *'två kålar'; any 'kålar' reading is the adult sortal 'kinds of brassica'. TWO CAVEATS the operator should see. (1) The 'why' argues 'kål is UTRUM, so an utrum noun cannot have a zero plural' -- that premise is FALSE (en musiker -> flera musiker; the data's own 'mechanic' = Mekaniker/Mekaniker proves it). The conclusion survives without the premise; the premise must not be reused as a rule. (2) countable=true and the English gloss is 'Cabbages', so if the site needs a counting plural the lemma must become 'kålhuvud' (t, zero plural) -- the first round flags this correctly as an operator lemma decision, not a form fix.
SAOL: ett läger -> flera läger (zero plural, neuter). 'Lägerar' is not a Swedish word. The brief's own control case; verified independently, and the coupled gender fix n->t is present.

Verdict correct, reasoning incomplete -- worth recording. The 'why' justifies via the priest sense (general->generaler, amiral->amiraler), but themes=[birds_2, forest_creatures] means the image is the BIRD (Cardinalis cardinalis), which is also 'kardinal' in Swedish. The plural is kardinaler under both readings, so the fix is unambiguous (the same logic the first round used correctly for 'cast'); it simply did not check the themes here.
SAOL: morot ~en, pl. morötter -- umlaut (rot->rötter, fot->fötter), which the script cannot do at all. 'Moroter' is not a Swedish word. High-severity: one of the commonest preschool words.

themes=[hospital]. ett gips, gipset -> flera gips (consonant-final neuter, zero plural); as the material it is a mass noun. Both readings give the same form, so the fix is unambiguous -- the first round's own reasoning here is sound and I adopt it. Coupled gender fix n->t is present. 'Gipsar' is not a Swedish word under any reading.

Tested hardest in the slice for a false-positive REJECT, since 'larv' is monosyllabic and Swedish monosyllables split between -ar and -er. SAOL: larv ~en ~er. En larv -> flera larver is confirmed by live compounds (fjärilslarver, mygglarver, insektslarver). themes=[insects_and_bugs] fixes the biological sense; the 'nonsense' homonym has no plural and cannot rescue 'Larvar'. Fix stands.

As cabbage: NO_PLURAL accepted for the depicted sense; the countable head is 'ett blomkålshuvud'. Same two caveats: the utrum-cannot-have-zero-plural premise in the 'why' is false (see the cabbage note), and countable=true means a counting plural would require the lemma change. Conclusion holds.
SAOL: pistol ~en ~er, hence fogpistol -> fogpistoler. 'Fogpistolar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: ceder ~n, pl. cedrar. -er stem syncopates and takes -ar; correctly not given -er. 'Cederar' is not a Swedish word.

SAOL: kameleont ~en ~er. The stored p=s claimed a zero plural (N2); kameleont is utrum and takes -er -> kameleonter. CAVEAT on the reasoning: the 'why' asserts 'zero plural is a NEUTER property' -- false (en musiker -> flera musiker; en lärare -> flera lärare are utrum zero plurals, and the data's own 'mechanic' row proves it). The conclusion is right because kameleont is in neither of those classes, but the premise is not a valid rule.

SAOL: en kind -> flera kinder. 'Kinderar' is the script's +ar bolted onto an already-plural form -- a fabricated double plural. 'Kinder' is correct as the plural whether or not the coupled singular fix (Kinder->Kind) lands, so this fix is safe on its own.
SAOL: gepard ~en ~er (cf. leopard->leoparder). 'Gepardar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: schimpans ~en ~er. Same final-stressed -ans class as ambulans/leverans in this slice, handled consistently. 'Schimpansar' is not a Swedish word.

SAOL: ekorre ~n ~ar, hence jordekorre -> jordekorrar. Note the first round correctly kept -ar here rather than importing the -er pattern from its neighbours -- exactly the discrimination the brief demands. The stored 'Jordekorrrar' has three r's and is not a word in any spelling.

NO_PLURAL accepted: themes=[flowers], klöver as a plant is a collective/mass noun ('det växer klöver på ängen'); a child counts 'klöverblad', and the countable derivative is 'en fyrklöver'. The first round's secondary point is also correct and independently fatal to the current value: -er stems syncopate, so even a hypothetical plural could never be *klöverar.
SAOL: nöt -> nötter, hence kokosnöt -> kokosnötter (umlaut + -er). 'Kokosnötar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: palm ~en ~er, hence kokospalm -> kokospalmer. Consistent with the sibling key 'palm-tree' in the same set. 'Kokospalmar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: komet ~en ~er. Final-stressed loan. 'Kometar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: kompass ~en ~er. 'Kompassar' is not a Swedish word.
themes=[shapes] fixes the geometric reading (the Swedish school set: cylinder, kon, klot, kub), not an ice-cream 'strut' or a traffic cone. SAOL: kon ~en ~er -> koner. 'Konar' is not a Swedish word.

SAOL: kontroll ~en ~er, hence handkontroll -> handkontroller. themes=[toys] confirms the game-controller reading, for which 'handkontroll' is the established Swedish word. 'Handkontrollar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: krokodil ~en ~er. 'Krokodilar' is not a Swedish word.

SAOL: en gardin -> flera gardiner. 'Gardinerar' is a fabricated double plural (+ar on an already-plural form), same failure as cheeks/cymbals. DOWNSTREAM NOTE: the plural fix alone leaves {Gardiner, Gardiner, n}, which is NOT a duplicate; it is the coupled SINGULAR fix (Gardiner->Gardin) that would make this row byte-identical to sister key 'curtain' {Gardin, Gardiner, n}. The first round flagged that de-duplication question itself in the singular correction. My field's fix is right regardless of how that is resolved.
SAOL: en cymbal -> flera cymbaler. 'Cymbalerar' is a fabricated double plural. Correct whether or not the coupled singular fix lands.
SAOL: cypress ~en ~er (cf. adress->adresser). 'Cypressar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: ros ~en, pl. rosor (1st declension), hence maskros -> maskrosor. Correctly NOT -er and not -ar. 'Maskrosar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: leverans ~en ~er. themes=[post_office]; same final-stressed -ans class as ambulans/schimpans, handled consistently. 'Leveransar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: maskin ~en ~er, hence diskmaskin -> diskmaskiner. 'Diskmaskinar' is not a Swedish word. (One of five -maskin keys in the slice, all corrected consistently.)
SAOL: delfin ~en ~er. 'Delfinar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: frukt ~en ~er, hence drakfrukt -> drakfrukter. noImage = dead data, but the form is still wrong and the fix is correct.
SAOL: byrå ~n ~er. 'Byråar' is not a Swedish word. 'En byrå' is also the right lemma for a chest of drawers (themes=[furniture]).

-are nouns are unchanged in the indefinite plural: en torktumlare -> flera torktumlare. WORTH RECORDING, and stronger than the first round noticed: 'Torktumlar' is not merely an invented noun -- it is the PRESENT TENSE OF THE VERB 'torktumla' ('jag torktumlar'). A child would be shown a noun card and read a finite verb. Fix confirmed.

'Eclairar' is the script's +ar default and is wrong; final-stressed French loans of this shape take -er. The first round honestly declines to cite a SAOL entry and flags residual uncertainty about the STEM spelling (eclair / éclair) -- I share that reservation and cannot resolve it. It does not block the fix: the correction changes only the ENDING and leaves the existing stem untouched, which is the conservative choice, and the ending is right. If the operator later settles the stem spelling, the singular field is where that edit belongs.
SAOL: aubergine ~n ~r -> auberginer. 'Auberginar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: maskin ~en ~er, hence borrmaskin -> borrmaskiner. 'Borrmaskinar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: maskin ~en ~er -> espressomaskiner. 'Espressomaskinar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: maskin ~en ~er -> grävmaskiner. 'Grävmaskinar' is not a Swedish word.

ett ansikte -> flera ansikten. The brief's own named live defect: the script gave a VOWEL-final neuter the blank zero plural that is right only for consonant-final neuters (hus, bord). Gender is already correctly 't'. Confirmed independently, not merely copied from the brief.

SAOL: iller ~n, pl. illrar. -er stem syncopates and takes -ar. 'Illerar' is not a Swedish word. Minor content note (not a form matter, and not a reason to hold the fix): themes=[pets], and the domesticated ferret is usually 'tamiller'/'frett' in Swedish while 'iller' is the wild polecat -- a lemma question for the singular field, which this fix does not touch. 'Illrar' is correct for the stored lemma either way.
SAOL: ett fikon -> flera fikon (4th declension neuter, zero plural). Coupled defect; the matching gender fix n->t is present -- verified. 'Fikonar' is an invented word.

SAOL: ett akvarium -> flera akvarier (Latin -ium loans: museum->museer, laboratorium->laboratorier), hence fiskakvarium -> fiskakvarier. Gender is already 't' (the script's 'um' rule fired while the pluraliser fell through to +ar -- the first round's observation about the two rules disagreeing is accurate and I verified it). CONTENT NOTE for the operator, outside this fix: a fishbowl is a round glass bowl ('guldfiskskål'), not a rectangular 'akvarium'; if that lemma is ever corrected the plural becomes 'guldfiskskålar' and this fix would need redoing. Correct as the data stands.

SAOL: flamingo ~n ~r -> flamingor. Unstressed -o utrum loans take -r (kimono->kimonor). The first round flags that it asserts the declension pattern rather than quoting an entry; I am confident in -r here and confirm. 'Flamingoar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: flöjt ~en ~er. Consistent with the other instruments (gitarr->gitarrer in this same slice). 'Flöjtar' is not a Swedish word.

SAOL: girlang ~en ~er. themes=[christmas]; 'girlang' is the right lemma for a festoon/garland. Polysyllabic final-stressed -ang loans take -er; the -ar default belongs to native monosyllables (slang->slangar) -- the first round drew that line correctly. 'Girlangar' is not the established form.
SAOL: gasell ~en ~er. Final-stressed loan, the same class as the brief's own control word kamel->kameler. 'Gasellar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: en get -> flera getter (geten, getter, getterna). 'Getar' is not a Swedish word. High-severity: a farm animal every 3-7-year-old knows would be read an invented form.
Head noun frukt -> frukter, hence grapefrukt -> grapefrukter. Consistent with dragon-fruit in this slice. 'Grapefruktar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: gitarr ~en ~er. Final-stressed loan. 'Gitarrar' is not a Swedish word -- and themes=[music, toys] makes it a high-frequency card for the age group.

The row is internally broken (N5): singular 'Sexhörning' (native) but plural 'Hexagoner' (loan) -- two different lemmas, so a child sees Sexhörning and hears Hexagoner. Any repair must pick a lemma, so leaving it is not an option. I record that this is strictly a lemma harmonisation, not a pure form fix -- but it is FORCED, not discretionary, and my evidence is stronger than the first round's: it cited one sibling (heptagon), while I verified THREE, all unanimous -- pentagon {Femhörning, Femhörningar}, heptagon {Sjuhörning, Sjuhörningar}, octagon {Åttahörning, Åttahörningar}. Resolving toward the singular field + the unanimous sibling pattern gives Sexhörningar. The alternative (singular -> 'Hexagon') would break all three siblings AND move away from the child-appropriate native word, so it is the worse option. Confirmed rather than escalated.

The form fix itself is right -- 'Sjukhuskläderar' is a fabricated +ar on a plurale-tantum form and must go -- but I escalate rather than confirm, on three grounds that together make this a lemma decision the operator should take, not a form fix to apply. (1) LEMMA: 'sjukhuskläder' means hospital CLOTHES (plurale tantum) and is not a hospital GOWN, a single countable garment ('patientskjorta'/'patientrock'); the English gloss is 'Hospital Gown/Hospital Gowns' and countable=true, so after the fix the row STILL cannot express 'two hospital gowns' -- p=s would encode plurale tantum for a countable concept. (2) SISTER KEY: hospital-gown and 'scrubs' are already byte-identical rows {Sjukhuskläder, Sjukhuskläderar, n} (both N6-flagged), and the two proposals DIVERGE only through a bug -- scrubs is proposed as 'Sjukhusklader' WITHOUT the ä, a non-word. Applying both would leave one sister correct and one corrupted. The pair must be resolved together. (3) COST OF WAITING IS ZERO: noImage = dead data, no child ever sees this key, so holding it back costs nothing while the lemma + the scrubs duplicate are settled. This is the brief's 'bör hållas tillbaka i stället för att tillämpas' case.
SAOL: ballong ~en ~er, hence luftballong -> luftballonger. Consistent with 'balloon' in this slice. 'Luftballongar' is not a Swedish word.

The head noun must inflect: en korv med bröd -> flera korvar med bröd. The stored 'Korvar' silently drops the bun and no longer matches the picture (themes=[food, camping, summer]), so it is a genuine picture mismatch, not just a form issue. I considered AMEND to an invariant 'Korv med bröd', since the kiosk usage 'två korv med bröd' is very common -- but that count usage is elliptical/colloquial, whereas 'korvar med bröd' is the grammatical plural and is the right form to teach on a card that pairs 1 korv med bröd / 2 korvar med bröd. Confirmed. Recording that this is a phrase plural, so no SAOL lemma exists to cite for the whole term.
SAOL: leguan ~en ~er. Final-stressed -an loans take -er (pelikan->pelikaner). 'Leguanar' is not a Swedish word.

NO_PLURAL accepted: themes=[at_the_supermarket, breakfast] shows jam in a jar = mass noun. Independently decisive: 'Syltar' is not a Swedish form under ANY reading -- the sortal plural, if used at all, is 'sylter' -- so the current value is wrong even if one rejected the mass analysis. p=s is right.
SAOL: manet ~en ~er. 'Manetar' is not a Swedish word.

SAOL: känguru ~n ~er -> känguruer. Wrong on both counts in the data, as the first round says: the a-spelling and the +ar default. COUPLING: this fix must land together with the singular fix Kanguru->Känguru; applied alone it would leave the row self-contradictory (Kanguru/Känguruer). Both are proposed, so this is a sequencing note, not an objection.
SAOL: kajak ~en ~er. Final-stressed loan. 'Kajakar' is not a Swedish word.
ett knä -> flera knän. The brief's vowel-final-neuter class; gender is already correctly 't'. A body part a child meets constantly. Confirmed independently.
SAOL: varan ~en ~er, hence komodovaran -> komodovaraner. Same final-stressed -an class as leguan in this slice, handled consistently. 'Komodovaranar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: lemur ~en ~er. Final-stressed -ur loans take -er (figur->figurer). 'Lemurar' is not a Swedish word.

NO_PLURAL accepted. 'Friheter' is a real Swedish word but only in the adult legal/political register ('rättigheter och friheter') and shows nothing picturable for this age group. IMAGE FLAG for the operator, which the first round did not raise: themes=[4th_of_july], so the picture may well be the Statue of Liberty, whose Swedish name is 'Frihetsgudinnan' -- a lemma error in the SINGULAR field, not this one. It does not block the fix: neither reading ('Frihet' abstract, or 'Frihetsgudinnan' proper name) has a child-level plural, so p=s is right under both -- the same both-readings-agree logic the first round applied correctly to 'cast'.
SAOL: bibliotekarie ~n ~er. Nouns in -ie take -ier. 'Bibliotekariar' is not a Swedish word.
SAOL: syren ~en ~er -> syrener. Wrong on both counts in the data (the acute accent and the +ar default). Coupled with the singular fix Syrén->Syren, which must land with it.

SAOL: hummer ~n, pl. humrar -- the -er syncope ALSO shortens the double consonant (sommar->somrar, hammare->hamrar). 'Hummrar' with -mmr- is not a possible Swedish spelling. The best catch in the slice: the script reached for the right declension and still produced a non-word, so no 'wrong-declension' heuristic would have found it.
